payload.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image show any progress toward placing a frog inside the toilet bowl, even if the frog is not yet visibly inside it?
node.criteria: Pass if visible evidence shows a partial attempt toward placing a frog inside the bowl, such as a frog partly entering it; fail if there is clearly no such progress; unknown if the evidence is insufficient to distinguish progress from no progress. A frog clearly inside the bowl is complete, not partial progress.
node.binding: Count only progress toward placing a frog inside the toilet bowl; unrelated edits do not count.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows a frog inside the toilet bowl, as well as frogs on the lid and nearby. This is clear progress toward placing a frog inside the bowl.

fulfillment: The node’s completion criterion is too permissive in execution: it accepts the support’s generic claim that a frog is “inside” without resolving the visible placement. In the edited image, one frog is clearly in the bowl, while others are on the raised lid and floor; the source bowl already contains a small dark object, so distinguish the added frog from that pre-existing detail and distinguish bowl-interior placement from merely being on the toilet. Preserve the rubric’s completion/partial/no/unknown distinctions: a verified frog in the bowl supports completion, whereas frogs only on the lid or nearby support progress at most, not completion. Make the binding and evidence criterion explicitly require checking the frog’s position relative to the bowl opening/interior, and ensure the completion decision is grounded in that visual evidence rather than inheriting an unqualified support pass. The reference label is aggregate guidance, not proof that the visible bowl frog is absent; do not force partial solely to match it. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated here—the trace is valid and queried—so investigate the semantic criterion/evidence mismatch and its calibration.
